headline: Replit Turns the Launch Video Into a Ten-Prompt Task
lede: Replit Animation, launched in February 2026, lets users generate polished product-explainer videos by describing what they want in plain language — no editing software, no motion designer required. The tool dispatches an AI agent that writes React animation code and renders it to an MP4, available on Replit's free tier. The poster's claim of a complete launch video in ten prompts is consistent with the documented workflow and points to a broader compression of creative production tasks.
body:
Replit Animation compresses what was once a motion-design engagement into a chat interface. Users describe the video they want — slides, transitions, backing music, narration — and an **AI agent** iterates until the output is ready to export as an MP4. The launch video @mattepstein assembled, with its Intro / Problem / Solution / Features structure, is a textbook product explainer: the kind of asset a startup might formerly have spent weeks and several thousand dollars producing through an agency.

The underlying architecture is not *generative video* in the manner of Runway. Replit's agent writes React-based animation code using the *Framer Motion* library and *SVG*, then renders each frame deterministically through a JavaScript shim that intercepts the browser's timing APIs before handing off to *FFmpeg* for final assembly. Because the output is source code rather than pixels, text, colors, and timing all remain editable after the initial generation run. Any live-action segments draw on Google's Veo 3.1 video-generation model.

The intelligence steering the agent is **Gemini 3.1 Pro**, announced by Google (GOOGL) DeepMind on February 19, 2026 — four days before Replit Animation's public debut. The model scores 77.1% on *ARC-AGI-2*, carries a one-million-token context window, and shows particular strength on SVG animation tasks. The timing reflects a deeper arrangement: Replit signed a multi-year partnership with Google Cloud in December 2025, becoming the cloud division's 2026 AI Tooling Partner of the Year; Microsoft (MSFT) holds a parallel deal for enterprise deployments on Azure. Together these agreements make Replit a proving ground for *vibe coding* — the AI-first development workflow, coined by AI researcher Andrej Karpathy, in which users describe intent in natural language rather than writing code by hand.

The competitive target is not Runway or professional video directors; it is Adobe (ADBE) After Effects and the motion-design agency — tools with a high skill floor and slow turnaround. Replit reports that Animation-made videos accumulated over ten million organic impressions in the tool's first weeks. At a free-tier price point and a ten-prompts benchmark, the question is less whether the tool works than how quickly the skill premium migrates further up the creative stack.

concepts.definition: A programming approach in which the user states intent in plain English and an AI agent generates the underlying code. Coined by AI researcher Andrej Karpathy, it has become the organizing concept for a wave of AI-first development tools aimed at non-engineers who want to build software without writing it themselves.

A software system that autonomously takes sequences of actions — writing code, testing it, revising, and repeating — to accomplish a user-specified goal, rather than simply responding to a single prompt. In Replit's case the agent loops through code generation and preview until the user approves the output.

A category of AI tool that synthesizes pixel sequences from text or image prompts using diffusion or similar machine-learning techniques. Tools such as Runway and Google Veo excel at cinematic and photorealistic content but produce non-editable video files, unlike Replit Animation's code-based approach.

An open-source React animation library that provides a declarative API for producing smooth animations and transitions in the browser. Replit Animation uses it as the backbone for its code-generated motion graphics.

Scalable Vector Graphics — an XML-based format for two-dimensional graphics that renders crisply at any resolution. Because SVG is code rather than pixels, it can be animated directly via JavaScript and CSS, making it well-suited to programmatic video generation.

A widely used open-source toolkit for encoding, decoding, and assembling audio and video. In Replit Animation it serves as the final step, combining deterministically rendered frames and Web Audio API output into an MP4 file.

A benchmark designed to test abstract reasoning and generalization in AI systems by presenting novel visual puzzles that resist pattern-matching from training data. A score of 77.1% for Gemini 3.1 Pro is cited as more than double its predecessor's result, signaling meaningful gains in general reasoning rather than mere knowledge retrieval.

A video-capture method in which all timing APIs in the browser are replaced by a controlled shim, so each frame is captured in a fixed sequence regardless of machine speed. This guarantees an identical, frame-accurate output on every run — unlike screen-recording, which can drop or duplicate frames under load.

Google DeepMind's video-generation model, used within the Replit Animation pipeline to supply any live-action video segments embedded in an otherwise code-generated output. It is part of the broader Google model stack that Replit accesses under its Google Cloud partnership.
